Sean,

Thanks for the demo earlier — ACME's security team had a few follow-ups about the private control plane (VPC) deployment. We want to make sure our identity and access model will map cleanly to our enterprise IdP. Quick list:

1) Can Redwood support assertion attributes for delegated operator roles? We currently send group claims and an 'entitlements' claim with custom URNs.
2) Does the private control plane expose a SCIM v2 endpoint for roster sync? We need a pull model and push model checklist.
3) How do you recommend handling service accounts that need cross-VPC operator privileges (no human SSO)?

Attached is a simple access matrix (acme-access-matrix.csv) — happy to walk through it on a call.

Priya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (inference infra) and Marissa (onboarding) to answer the technicals and ops steps. Quick answers up-front:

- Yes, we can map custom group/entitlement claims to operator role bindings in the private control plane. We support claim-to-role rules as part of the SAML assertion mapping (documented in redwood-scim-endpoints.md).
- SCIM v2: we support both push (we accept SCIM POST/PUT from your IdP) and periodic pull/webhook sync patterns — Ben will enumerate supported subset.
- Service accounts: we recommend short-lived operator tokens issued via our token-exchange flow backed by your KMS; details below.

Can we schedule a 45-minute call tomorrow to go through mapping examples and a minimal acceptance checklist? I'm free 11:00–14:00 PT.

—Sean

Hi Priya,

I'll be on the call with the specifics but here's a concise tech summary so your engineers can review beforehand:

SAML assertion mapping
- Supported attributes: NameID, email, groups (as array), entitlements (RFC-compliant JSON string) and custom attributes.
- Mapping rules: simple regex->role, prefix matching (e.g., 'acme:admin' -> role:operator.admin), and a fallback mapping for 'external:contractor' that limits runtime privileges.

SCIM
- Endpoints: /scim/v2/Users, /scim/v2/Groups. We implement PATCH (RFC7644), bulk operations not supported in private control plane current GA.
- Modes: push (your IdP calls our /scim/v2), and pull (we call your SCIM endpoint using an OAuth client credential grant). For pull we support incremental sync using 'if-modified-since' headers and startIndex pagination.

Service accounts
- Short-lived operator tokens via token-exchange (OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange RFC7523 flow) with optional mTLS for the token endpoint.
- Recommended pattern: create a scoped service identity in your IdP, map that identity to a constrained operator role in our control plane, and require rotation via your KMS/HSM.

I've attached a short internal doc (redwood-scim-endpoints.md) with example payloads and mapping snippets.

Cheers,
Ben

Thanks — couple of clarifying items from our infra team after reading Ben's note:

- For pull-mode SCIM, what OAuth scope/aud claim should our token have? We run a short-lived client credential token (15m). Also, do you accept JWTs signed by our private CA or only standard OAuth JWTs?
- For the token-exchange flow, can Redwood accept constrained claims (eg 'session_max_ttl' or 'delegation_audience') to prevent privilege escalation?

Also, can you add a line in the engagement checklist about SAML cert rotation cadence and expected downtime for metadata reload in private control plane? Our compliance team wants explicit windows.

Tom
Principal Infra Engineer, ACME

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-06T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions: private CP assertion mapping and operator access

Tom/Priya — answers inline and next steps below.

- OAuth scope for pull-mode SCIM: use scope 'scim.read' and audience 'redwood-scim'. We accept JWTs signed by your CA if they're presented as a JWT bearer token per RFC7523; we also support standard opaque tokens via client credentials.
- Token-exchange: yes — we accept constrained claims including 'session_max_ttl' and 'delegation_audience' as part of the exchange payload. We validate them against your mapped policy and will reject overly broad requests.
- SAML cert rotation: recommended cadence is 90 days. Metadata reload in private control plane is rolling by tenant; typical propagation is 2–7 minutes if you push new metadata to our control plane API. We'll include a scheduled maintenance window if a private on-prem control plane is air-gapped — Marissa to own the checklist item.

Next steps / action items:
1) Marissa to share detailed acceptance checklist and runbook (I attached a stub: soc2-evidence-stub.pdf to show where audit items live).
2) Ben to provide a sample JWT for pull-mode SCIM and a token-exchange example
3) ACME to confirm preferred call slot; Sean will send calendar invite.

We'll follow up with a recorded run-through and example payloads.
